_why: The four rules the Node driver's user.js writer follows, FROZEN. Until 2026-08-28 prefs_byte_parity.py read them out of src/invisible_playwright/_driver/package/lib/coreBundle.js on every run, deliberately, so that an upstream change moved the gate with it instead of leaving it comparing against a stale transcription. The bundle is being deleted with the Node driver, so the derived fact becomes a recorded one - and this file exists to make that visible rather than silent.
_how_to_verify: While a bundle is still reachable, prefs_byte_parity.py re-extracts and compares against these values, and FAILS on a mismatch. To reach one after the deletion: git worktree add <dir> <the last commit that carried _driver/>, then point the gate at it with INVPW_DRIVER_BUNDLE=<dir>/src/invisible_playwright/_driver/package/lib/coreBundle.js.
_what_a_stale_copy_would_cost: The gate would compare our writer against our own idea of the driver, which always agrees. That is the failure mode the run-time read existed to prevent, and it is why the provenance below is recorded to the byte instead of just being dated.
